name: Ironveil Disgraced CorpSec Bouncer's Door Rig
description: A stripped Brightline corporate security jacket with all insignia cut off — the ghost outlines of rank patches still visible as darker rectangles on the sleeve. Underneath, a plain black compression mock-neck that hides a spinal augmentation rig up to C4. Tactical trousers with the knee-armor pockets emptied out and re-stuffed with a flask and a burner comm. One boot is standard-issue military; the other is a mismatched Shelf replacement.
functionality: Residual ballistic-weave in jacket provides light protection; spinal rig channel remains fully functional under the mock-neck.
what_it_says: Someone who used to have authority and now enforces someone else's door for Φ12 an hour.
story_hooks: The rank patch outlines are from a Brightline division that was publicly dissolved after a massacre — anyone who knows CorpSec history will recognize it.
The emptied knee-armor pockets once held classified hardware that this person quietly kept and hid elsewhere.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately desecrated uniform that screams 'former authority stripped of rank.' The jacket drapes with institutional memory—cut-away patches create a negative-space narrative of disgrace. Underneath, the compression mock-neck hints at internal augmentation without flaunting it. Asymmetrical boots ground the look in survival pragmatism.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, slightly oversized through the torso to accommodate spinal rig; compression shirt is skin-tight; trousers are tactical-cut with reinforced thighs and modified pockets
physical_description.primary_material: Jacket: ballistic weave (original Brightline synthetic-reinforced canvas, now faded); compression shirt: medical-grade spandex blend; trousers: ripstop poly-cotton with kevlar threading; boots: mismatched (military synthetic leather vs. Shelf recycled composite)
physical_description.texture: Jacket fabric is broken-in rough, deliberately abraded where patches were excised; compression shirt is smooth and form-fitting; trousers have a utilitarian matte finish with stress wrinkles; boots show mixed wear—one glossy and maintained, one scuffed and salvaged
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: charcoal and ash gray jacket with ghost-pale rectangular outlines where insignia lived; black compression mock-neck; slate trousers; boots are contrasting—one deep chrome-black, one gunmetal gray with streaks of oxidation
physical_description.closures: Jacket: friction-fit + magnetic snaps (some deactivated); compression shirt: friction-fit; trousers: magnetic waistband with reinforced belt loops; boots: lace + velcro hybrid (one clean, one deteriorating)
distinctive_features: Deliberately cut-away rank patches with ghost-shadow rectangles still visible—the primary visual scar
Modified knee-armor pockets now housing a flask and burner comm instead of ballistic plating
Compression mock-neck bulging subtly at the nape where spinal augmentation rig terminates at C4
One pristine military-issue boot vs. one scuffed Shelf replacement—visual asymmetry as defiance
Faded Brightline branding barely visible on shoulder seam, intentionally left unhidden as reminder
Wear patterns concentrated at wrists, elbows, and collar—signs of restraint and struggle
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 transitioning to Tier 4—once Tier 1-2 corporate, now street-functional salvage
physical_description.cultural_context: A fallen corpo security operative; someone who was purged, demoted, or walked away. The outfit broadcasts 'I know the system and was discarded by it.' Wearing this is an act of refusal—rejecting the erasure by wearing the evidence of it. Street credibility through institutional scar tissue.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately weathered; the jacket is treated with intentional wear patterns (not accidental decay); the compression shirt is meticulously maintained because the augmentation inside depends on it; trousers are functional and patched at stress points; boots are a study in contrasts—one obsessively cleaned, one intentionally neglected
